items.prompt: A pupil says a magnet will attract any metal object. What is wrong with this idea?
items.answer: No: a magnet only pulls iron and a few metals, and ignores most other metals
choices: Yes: if it is a metal, a magnet will pull it
No: a magnet only pulls iron and a few metals, and ignores most other metals
Yes: a magnet pulls every object, metal or not
items.misconceptionCode: A magnet attracts every kind of metal.

items.prompt: A child drags a box towards herself across the floor. Which force is she using?
items.answer: A pull, because the box is brought closer to the child
choices: A push, because the box moves across the table
A pull, because the box is brought closer to the child
Friction, because the box is sliding

items.prompt: A block slides down a rough slope and slows down. Name the force that slows it and explain how it works.
items.answer: Friction is the rubbing force between the block and the rough surface; it pushes back against the slide and slows the block down.

items.prompt: Kicking a football: is this a push or a pull? Give the reason.
items.answer: It is a push: the foot pushes the ball away.

items.prompt: Two magnets are brought together with their north poles facing each other. What happens?
items.answer: They push each other apart and repel
choices: They push each other apart and repel
Nothing: magnets only work when they are touching

items.prompt: In one sentence, say what two magnets do when the north pole of one faces the north pole of the other.
items.answer: They repel: like poles push each other apart.
